nodes.title: Harness engineering: cheaper gates, clearer refusals, less drift

acceptance: orchestration.yaml policy gains max_fix_rounds (default unset = current behaviour); after that many blocking rounds on one leaf, handoff status reports fix_round_budget_spent and names the command that resolves it

rca-record.schema.json gains recommended_action.type defer_findings; a reviewer finding whose input class was not named in any earlier round of the leaf may be listed under it, each with a proposed follow-up leaf title and acceptance line

A human-only command (refuses unattended/agent runs the same way mark-implementation-reviewed --yes does for self-review) applies a defer_findings record: it adds the follow-up leaf with add-node, writes a decisions.yaml entry naming the deferred findings and the approver, and the review gate then counts the deferring reviewer's block at that commit as resolved; every other block still counts
A finding on an input class an earlier round already named, or any finding marked correctness on a previously passing acceptance id, can never be deferred; a test pins both refusals
docs/orchestration-review.md and the RCA design note document the budget, the deferral and the audit trail; nothing changes for projects that leave max_fix_rounds unset
nodes.title: A review fix-round budget that defers new-input-class findings to a follow-up leaf

acceptance: remove-dependency accepts a display id exactly as add-dependency does; naming a dependency the node does not list exits 1 and names the node's actual dependencies (no more '[ok] … did not list' with exit 0)
mark-implementation-reviewed's 'working tree is not clean' refusal lists the offending paths (at most 20, then a count) and says how to clear them
abort-task-pickup's worktree hint gives a command that works on the worktree pickup left (it accounts for the untracked work/brief-<ID>.md pickup writes), and a test runs the printed command

docs/contributor-guide.md states the rule (a non-zero exit prints what failed, why, and the next command to run) and a parametrized test runs each refusal above through the CLI and asserts the message names a runnable next step
nodes.title: Every refusal names its fix

acceptance: specy-road garden (or chore garden) runs read-only scans and prints one finding per line: docs/*.md and agent files naming a command this version does not register (extending validate_stale_commands beyond AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md; flags are out of scope, since no per-command flag registry exists), enforced-rule comments marked 'enforced: advisory' in managed agent files, and ratchet baselines (policy.ratchet_paths) that grew since the last tag

--open-chores turns each finding class into at most one chore leaf (title, acceptance, touch zones from the finding paths) through the existing chore/add-node path, never edits code itself, and is idempotent: a second run with the same findings adds nothing
A cadence key (like research/ cadences) lets validate say when gardening is due; docs/orchestration-chores.md documents the scans, the cadence and how to run it unattended
nodes.title: Scheduled gardening chores that find drift and open small chore leaves
Quality signals agents and PMs read first

acceptance: Each leaf's gate commit (mark-implementation-reviewed) carries a 'Review-tally:' trailer recording its review rounds, blocks, findings per category, integrity findings and RCA escalations, built in a new specy_road/review_tally.py and added through review_gate.commit_trailers with at most a one-line call (review_gate.py is at its line cap); roadmap-context.md gains a 'Quality by area' section: per touch-zone prefix (top-level directory under the project, configurable depth), leaves landed, mean review rounds per leaf, block rate, integrity findings and RCA escalations, over the last N completed leaves (default 50), computed only from those trailers in tracked git history, never from gitignored work/reviews/, so digest --check gives the same result on every machine and in CI; leaves landed before the trailer existed are counted as 'no tally' and excluded from rates
Areas worse than a policy threshold are listed first with the numbers; digest --check stays deterministic (no timestamps or wall-clock inputs); empty history prints nothing
orchestrate plan may route strong_review to a leaf whose touch zones fall in a flagged area when policy.quality_routing is on (default off); a test pins both settings
nodes.title: Per-area quality scores in the digest from review history

acceptance: roadmap/debt.yaml (schema shipped with init project and refresh-schemas) holds entries {id, title, found_in (node id or free text), paths, severity, status open|planned|closed, node (when planned)}; specy-road debt add|list|close manage it without hand edits
specy-road debt plan <id> --under <PARENT> creates the leaf through add-node, links it, and marks the entry planned; closing the leaf (finish-this-task) closes the entry
roadmap-context.md lists open debt by severity (at most 10 lines); validate warns on an entry whose linked node no longer exists
nodes.title: A tracked tech-debt ledger that planning can turn into leaves

acceptance: specy-road models stats prints per reviewer model, over the last N recorded reviews (default 50): reviews, block rate, approvals overturned (another model blocked the same commit and the leaf then changed), mean probes per approve (M14.5 when present) and mean commands_rerun lines, from local review records and the tracked Review-tally trailers M12.4.1 adds

With policy.evidence_scoring on (default off), orchestrate plan lowers a reviewer's score when its overturned-approval rate exceeds a policy threshold and says so in the plan; off leaves plans unchanged; a test pins both
Out of scope: the digest (per-area scores are M12.4.1) and changing the roster automatically
nodes.title: Per-model review evidence: block rate and overturned approvals feed orchestrate plan

acceptance: specy-road worktree cleanup <ID>, run from the main checkout after finish-this-task lands the leaf, first moves leaf-local hand-off files (work/reviews/<ID>/** in the leaf's worktree, including history/ copies and RUN-* logs) into the shared hand-off directory (reviews_root), never overwriting a different file (it keeps both, the moved one with a suffix); then terminates the leaf's worker if one is idle and removes the worktree; a test puts a review history file only in the leaf worktree's ignored work/reviews/<ID>/history/ and asserts it exists in the main checkout's hand-off dir after cleanup and the worktree is gone

cleanup refuses, removes nothing and prints one line per reason when the worktree has commits not on the integration branch, uncommitted changes or untracked files git does not ignore, or ignored files outside a known-regenerable list (__pycache__ and tool caches, node_modules, work/prompt-*.md, work/brief-*.md, work/.on-complete-*.yaml, .specyrd/cache/) once hand-off files are moved; reuses worktree_prune.plan_prune (including M14.3's foreign-worktree refusal) and worker terminate; a test per refusal

specy-road worktree sweep [--dry-run] lists every linked worktree (wherever it lives, e.g. under .claude/worktrees/ or a temp dir) whose branch or detached HEAD is contained in the integration branch, with no registry claim (so never a claimed or deferred leaf's), no live or resumable worker, no live session, and nothing unsaved by the cleanup rules; it removes each (moving hand-off files first) or with --dry-run only reports; output is one line per worktree: removed, would remove, or kept with the reason; it uses M14.2's live-leaf rules rather than a copy; a test with a claimed, a live-session, a dirty and a removable worktree pins the four lines

grind-session runs cleanup after each leaf it lands, and policy.worktree_sweep (off by default; between_leaves) makes it run sweep between leaves; the specyrd-orchestrate command tells the coordinator to run worktree cleanup <ID> after finish and worktree sweep --dry-run at the start of a session; docs/orchestration-chores.md documents both

Out of scope: deleting remote branches (never); local branch deletion only with --delete-local-branch, only for a branch the integration branch contains; cleaning the main checkout's work/ files (finish-this-task's cleanup already owns those)

worktree cleanup and sweep also end the session presence records tied to the removed worktree or its deleted branch (the leaf's worker, reviewer and session entries), so session list shows none for a landed leaf; a test with a leftover reviewer and session record asserts both are gone after cleanup

sweep removes a pickup-created worktree whose branch the integration branch contains (the reported case: it stayed after finish, and branch pruning skipped its branch as '(worktree)'), and after removal the branch is no longer skipped; a test covers it

docs/orchestration-chores.md warns that gh pr merge --delete-branch can remove a leaf's branch while its worktree still holds uncommitted or ignored hand-off files, and says to run worktree cleanup <ID> (which saves hand-off files first) before deleting the branch
nodes.title: The orchestrator cleans up landed leaves and stale worktrees automatically, saving hand-off files first

acceptance: Every command specy_road/cli.py registers (its dispatch tables) yields its argparse parser without running the command, through a build_parser() (or equivalent) that specy_road/cli_parsers.py reaches by command name, including nested subcommands (review record, worker delegate, handoff status …); a parity test walks every registered command and subcommand and fails naming any that yields no parser; cli.py itself grows by at most two lines

The stale-command scan in validate, and M12.3's garden scan through the same function, reports each 'specy-road <cmd> [<sub>] --flag' mention in the files it already scans whose flag that command or subcommand does not accept, as file:line, the command, the unknown flag and the closest valid flag (difflib); valid flags, short options and flags after a bare -- are not reported; a fixture with one stale and one valid flag pins the output

Commands that take free-form passthrough arguments are exempt by declaration, not by guess: a parser that uses argparse.REMAINDER or a declared passthrough group (grind-session's implement-hook passthrough), and anything after a bare --, is not checked, and the exemption list is printed by the parity test; behaviour of every command is unchanged
Out of scope: whether a valid flag's behaviour changed (M13.8's behaviour-change catalogue), checking flag values, and prose mentions without a specy-road command
nodes.title: Every command exposes its parser, and the stale-command scan reports flags a command does not accept
